# Prepared-print fixtures

These are checked-in files, not generated at test runtime. Each `.gcode.3mf` is
a real ZIP/3MF container with `[Content_Types].xml`, `_rels/.rels`,
`3D/3dmodel.model`, and the `Metadata/` members its slicer would write. They were
produced once with Python's `zipfile` (fixed 2025-01-01 timestamps) and the
`.gcode`/`.bgcode` files were written alongside them, so the parser always works
against stable bytes.

Every container carries the real package relationship in `_rels/.rels`:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><Relationships xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships"><Relationship Target="/3D/3dmodel.model" Id="rel0" Type="http://schemas.microsoft.com/3dmanufacturing/2013/01/3dmodel"/></Relationships>
```

and names the slicer that wrote it in the model metadata:

```xml
<metadata name="Application">PrusaSlicer-2.8.1</metadata>
```

| File | Provenance |
| --- | --- |
| `prusaslicer_mk3s.gcode.3mf` | 3MF ZIP with text `Metadata/Slic3r_PE.config` and a `Metadata/plate_1.gcode` header generated by PrusaSlicer 2.8.1; `Application` is `PrusaSlicer-2.8.1`. |
| `orca_x1c.gcode.3mf` | 3MF ZIP with JSON `Metadata/project_settings.config` (Bambu-flavoured: `Bambu Lab X1 Carbon` machine and a `bambu_studio_version` entry) and an OrcaSlicer 2.1.0 `Metadata/plate_1.gcode` header, pinning OrcaSlicer before Bambu Studio. `Application` is `OrcaSlicer-2.1.0`, so the Orca label also comes from the container metadata. |
| `bambu_p1s.gcode.3mf` | 3MF ZIP with JSON `Metadata/project_settings.config`, XML `Metadata/slice_info.config` prediction, and a Bambu Studio g-code header; `Application` is `BambuStudio-01.09.02.57`. |
| `cura_ender3.gcode` | Plain Cura 5.6.0 header text. |
| `simplify3d.gcode` | Plain Simplify3D 5.1.2 header text using comma separators. |
| `unknown.gcode` | Plausible g-code with no generator or settings comments, so every fact is unknown. |
| `prusa_bgcode.bgcode` | Structurally valid Prusa binary G-code: `GCDE` magic, little-endian `uint32` version `1`, little-endian `uint16` checksum type `0`, then one uncompressed GCode block — `uint16` type `7`, `uint16` compression `0`, `uint32` uncompressed size (the compressed-size field is omitted when compression is `0`, per libbgcode), and the ASCII g-code comments as the block payload. `file(1)` reports `Binary G-code Version 1, no checksum`. |

The parser must always produce exactly these facts:

| File | printer | material | nozzle_mm | layer_height_mm | estimated_seconds | slicer / format |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prusaslicer_mk3s.gcode.3mf` | Prusa MK3S+ | PLA | 0.4 | 0.2 | 11520 | PrusaSlicer / gcode_3mf |
| `orca_x1c.gcode.3mf` | Bambu Lab X1 Carbon | PLA | 0.4 | 0.2 | None | OrcaSlicer / gcode_3mf |
| `bambu_p1s.gcode.3mf` | Bambu Lab P1S | PLA | 0.4 | 0.2 | 11520 | Bambu Studio / gcode_3mf |
| `cura_ender3.gcode` | Ender-3 | PLA | 0.4 | 0.2 | 11520 | Cura / gcode |
| `simplify3d.gcode` | Prusa MK3S | PLA | 0.4 | 0.2 | None | Simplify3D / gcode |
| `unknown.gcode` | None | None | None | None | None | unknown / gcode |
| `prusa_bgcode.bgcode` | Prusa MK3S+ | PLA | 0.4 | 0.2 | 11520 | PrusaSlicer / bgcode |
